sources.entry: SafeLine - Web application firewall / reverse proxy to protect your web apps from attacks and exploits. (Demo, Source Code) GPL-3.0 Docker
SafeLine | Web application firewall and reverse proxy to protect web apps

summary.one_liner: SafeLine is a self-hosted web application firewall (WAF) and reverse proxy that filters HTTP traffic in front of web apps to block attacks and exploits.
summary.what_it_does: SafeLine sits between clients and a web application as a reverse proxy and filters and monitors HTTP/S traffic. The README says it defends against web attacks such as SQL injection, XSS, code injection, OS command injection, CRLF injection, XXE, SSRF, path traversal, and others. It offers IP-based rate limiting to throttle DoS, brute-force, and traffic-surge abuse. Its anti-bot challenge lets human users through while blocking crawlers and bots. It also provides an authentication challenge that requires visitors to enter a password, a Web Access Control List, and dynamic protection that encrypts HTML and JS on each visit. The README includes a comparison table against ModSecurity and Cloudflare Free, which is the project's own evaluation.
use_cases: Block SQL injection and XSS attacks on a website
Stop bots and scrapers from hitting a web app
Add a password gate in front of a website
Protect a self-hosted web app behind a reverse proxy
how_to_run: Information on how to install SafeLine can be found in the Install Guide (linked from the README; the README itself gives no commands)
notable: Self-hosted WAF and reverse proxy covering a broad list of OWASP-style attack classes
Dynamic protection that encrypts HTML and JS on each visit
Anti-bot challenge and password-based authentication challenge for visitors
Ecosystem integrations: MCP server, Ingress-NGINX plugin, Kong Gateway plugin
caveats: README warns that installing the international edition may fail to connect to cloud services for users in mainland China; a Chinese-language install guide is referenced
A PRO edition with paid plans is offered alongside the open-source edition
Effectiveness figures come from the project's own evaluation table
